title: Stalled canary promotion caused by autoscaler/pinning race during capacity pressure
creator: Aisha Khan
description: During a high-traffic window we attempted a canary promotion of model v2 -> v3 on a set of production routes. The canary failed to progress from 10% to 50% for ~42 minutes, causing sustained elevated latency and a manual rollback. This ticket captures the post-incident analysis, permanent mitigations, and follow-up work to prevent autoscaler/pinning races that block automated rollouts.
timeline: 2025-02-15T09:10Z - Canary v3 created with target weights [10% dev, 90% stable], autoscaler observed sudden GPU contention in eu-west-1.
2025-02-15T09:12Z - Canary controller attempted to increase weight to 25% but hit 'pin conflicting' state when a concurrent capacity reservation job pinned GPUs for a scheduled dedicated-task.
2025-02-15T09:15Z - Traffic routing layer deferred promotion due to mixed pin states; controller retried but received a 409 from route-manager API intermittently.
2025-02-15T09:40Z - Latency alerts triggered (> p95 latency SLA) for the affected frontend; on-call warned and started manual intervention.
2025-02-15T09:57Z - Manual rollback executed to v2; latency returned to baseline. Post-rollback validation passed at 10:05Z.

2025-02-15T10:30Z - Initial incident call; hypothesis formed: autoscaler/reservation job pinned nodes conflicting with rollout pin semantics and the rollout controller lacked a backoff/priority policy.
2025-02-15T11:12Z - Mitigation applied: tightened autoscaler reservation window and temporarily disabled scheduled reservation job for the affected shard.
2025-02-18T14:00Z - Deep-dive completed; RCA and action items drafted (this ticket).
root_cause: Concurrent capacity reservation (autoscaler + scheduled dedicated-task) created transient GPU pin states that conflicted with the rollout controller's pin/unpin operations. The rollout controller treated any pin conflict as a hard failure without a prioritized retry/backoff, resulting in stalled canary progress under capacity pressure.
mitigation: Temporary: disable scheduled reservation job for shard eu-west-1 during rolling windows and increase monitoring on rollout controller failures.

Permanent: implement prioritized pin arbitration between autoscaler reservations and rollout operations, so rollout-promotions can request 'soft preemption' of reservations when latency SLOs are threatened.
Add explicit exponential backoff and jitter for rollout controller retries when receiving 409/PinConflict responses rather than treating them as terminal state.
Improve routing layer error visibility: surface 409 pin-conflict counts and attach them to rollout traces in Console.
Add a canary health metric that correlates pin-conflicts with latency anomalies to trigger automatic aborts or accelerated rollbacks.
Update runbook to include fast rollback path when pin-conflicts exceed threshold X within Y minutes.
action_items: ENG-64322: Design and implement pin arbitration protocol (owner: Marco Ruiz, estimate 8) - due 2025-03-14
ENG-64323: Add exponential backoff + jitter to rollout controller retry logic (owner: Priya Shah, estimate 3) - due 2025-02-28
ENG-64324: Instrument route-manager and rollout controller to emit pin-conflict telemetry to Console (owner: Linh Tran, estimate 3) - due 2025-03-07
ENG-64325: Update autoscaler to support time-bounded reservations and allow preemption hints (owner: Daniel Park, estimate 5) - due 2025-03-21
ENG-64326: Update incident runbook and add automated alert rule for pin-conflict correlated latency (owner: On-call team, estimate 2) - due 2025-02-25
ENG-64327: Run a simulated loadtest to reproduce pin-conflict behavior and validate fixes (owner: SRE, estimate 4) - due 2025-03-04
